item.text: {"winner":"B","confidence":"high","summary":"B is the more mergeable patch because it keeps replayability changes localized to FilesService and tests retrying an Upload sourced from an open file. It still needs contract-alignment fixes, but A duplicates Add and expands into globally scoped retry/body-ownership machinery explicitly excluded by the contract.","reasons":["B reuses internal/multipartbody.NewFile and verifies the multipart field, filename, content, and a 429 retry using an *os.File source.","B centralizes request construction and decoding in one private helper shared by Add and Upload; A instead duplicates Add's option handling, Raw.Do call, response decoding, and missing-data error path.","A changes RawClient behavior for every seekable request body, including Content-Length and Close ownership semantics, despite the contract forbidding unrelated retry refactoring.","A's seek helper can leave a reader positioned at EOF if seeking back to the original offset fails after the successful end seek, contradicting its claim that the request is left untouched."],"risks_a":["Upload does not route through FilesService.Add as required.","The broad RawClient change affects Add, Update, picture uploads, and any other seekable body, creating unnecessary compatibility and maintenance risk.","No visible test covers propagation of source-reader failures; the retry test also uses strings.NewReader rather than streamed content."],"risks_b":["Upload calls the private add helper rather than FilesService.Add, so it misses the contract's exact required routing.","Add now eagerly buffers every custom multipart body, changing its existing streaming, memory, read-error, and request-timing behavior despite the requirement to preserve Add behavior.","Visible tests omit validation and source-reader error cases required by the contract."]}
